[ASSISTANT_SAID] Jean Baudrillard was known for his theories on hyperreality and simulacra.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Gilles Deleuze was known for his work on poststructuralism and becoming.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Baudrillard believed that in postmodern society, the distinction between reality and representation has become blurred.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Baudrillard argued that simulations and representations dominate our understanding of the world.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Deleuze would argue that reality is constantly in flux.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Deleuze believed the role of the philosopher is to think through and make sense of becoming.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Baudrillard's argument in the debate: "In postmodern society, we are surrounded by simulations and representations that have come to dominate our understanding of the world. Reality has been replaced by a hyperreal, a world of images and signs that exists independently of the real world. We no longer have a relationship to the real, but instead live in a world of illusions and spectacle."  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Deleuze's argument in the debate: "I disagree. Reality is not something static or fixed, but is constantly in flux. We cannot understand the world through representation or simulation, but must instead think through the becoming of things. The role of the philosopher is not to represent the world, but to think through the processes of change and transformation that constitute reality."  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Baudrillard's counterargument: "But how can we think about becoming when we are surrounded by simulations and representations that obscure our relationship to the real? We are no longer able to differentiate between the real and the fake, and as a result, we are trapped in a world of illusion."  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Deleuze's response: "I would argue that the distinction between the real and the fake is not as clear-cut as you suggest. Reality is not something fixed or static, but is constantly in flux. We must reject the idea of representation and instead focus on the processes of becoming that constitute reality."  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] Baudrillard's further challenge: "But isn't that just a form of escapism? By focusing on becoming and refusing to engage with representation, aren't we just avoiding the problems of postmodern society?"
